hypothesis: The O(2) matter sector of the parent action, with chi = the He-4 atom and the quartic fixed by the measured He-He scattering length (lam = 8 pi a m, wave SI-1), describes He II at tree level: its sound speed c = hbar sqrt(4 pi a n)/m equals the measured first sound. This is the lane Topic 13 used when it identified Phi with the He II superfluid fraction.

observable.quantity: first sound speed u1 of He II
observable.domain: liquid He-4, T90 = 1.70 K, saturated vapour pressure

prediction_method.description: n = rho/m_He4; c(a) = hbar sqrt(4 pi a n)/m_He4 evaluated at a - sigma_minus and a + sigma_plus; D = 0 if u1 lies between them, else the smaller fractional distance of the two ends from u1. n a^3 is reported but is not a criterion.

fixed_parameters: lam = 8 pi a m (tree level, no loop or beyond-mean-field correction)
u1 = 233.1 m/s at 1.70 K (Donnelly and Barenghi 1998)
fail_criterion: D > 0.30 -> FAILED for this lane; 0.10 < D <= 0.30 -> INCONCLUSIVE
note: Disclosure: not blind. The outcome was computed before drafting (wave SI-1 and the draft discussion): c is about 850 m/s against u1 = 233.1 m/s and n a^3 is about 2.5e4, so FAILED is expected. The value of the card is to record that failure under a rule fixed in advance, which settles whether Topic 13's He-4 Phi lane can come from the parent action. The 10 percent and 30 percent thresholds are AI-chosen; tree-level corrections scale as sqrt(n a^3), so no model error is defined for a dense fluid and the author should judge the thresholds. A failure applies only to this lane (chi = atom, tree level); it says nothing about the chi = nucleon lane of T005 or about a phenomenological two-fluid closure. Not UET-distinct: standard dilute-gas theory fails He II in the same way. The comparison script has not been run.
